source.title: Unified Multimodal Discrete Diffusion
source.authors: Alexander Swerdlow; Mihir Prabhudesai; Siddharth Gandhi; Deepak Pathak; Katerina Fragkiadaki

record.tranche_reason: It conducts an IsoFLOP scaling analysis on joint image-text models, extending scaling analysis to unified multimodal discrete diffusion. It also includes an autoregressive comparison.
record.gate_note: The scaling results are the IsoFLOP analysis in Figure 3 and its stated 13.2x compute-efficiency comparison. Other scaling references in the text are background citations, not this study's results. The reported 1.4B model's qualitative demonstrations are not scaling-law results.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own IsoFLOP sweep (13 sizes, 34M–1290M non-embedding parameters, C≈6ND) on joint image-text discrete diffusion and AR models, and fits compute-optimal parameter counts. This is a new setting for V3 and V5. The results appear only in Figure 3: no exponents, budgets or loss values are stated in the text, so no verdict can be read from them.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors report an IsoFLOP analysis finding UniDisc needs about 13.2x more training compute than AR to reach the same loss. The claim that UniDisc 'scales well across parameters and dataset size' (Section 4.4) is qualitative, backed only by training a 1.4B model. The paper's main conclusion is that UniDisc beats AR in inference efficiency, generation quality and controllability, not anything about scaling-law form.
record.recipe_differences: Uses an IsoFLOP analysis with fixed-compute sweeps and fitted compute-optimal parameter counts, but applies it to joint image-text models, including discrete diffusion, rather than language-only autoregressive models. UniDisc's joint perplexity is an upper bound, whereas the AR baseline's is an exact likelihood.
record.method_sensitivity: The compared training objectives and attention masks differ between UniDisc and AR. Appendix F reports ablations of design choices, but does not establish that scaling-law fits or compute-optimal allocation change under those choices.

fits_no_version.finding: At matched joint validation loss, UniDisc (masked discrete diffusion) needs about 13.2x the training compute of an otherwise identical AR model on image-text data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-objective choice (diffusion vs AR) shifts the compute-loss scaling curve by a large constant factor in unified image-text training.

record.problems: Scaling-curve values and compute-optimal parameter counts are shown only in figures, with no numerical values or fit exponents stated in the text. The compared loss measures differ in status: UniDisc perplexity is an upper bound, while AR perplexity is an exact likelihood.

untested.parts: No language-only loss scaling. The joint image-text loss scaling shape is not reported numerically.
No extrapolation from small fits to much larger runs. The 1.4B model is not compared with a predicted loss.
No exponent is reported for optimal N vs C. Optimal token count is not reported. There is no comparison with Kaplan or Chinchilla splits.
Shape is not varied at fixed parameter count. Table 2 variants differ in both size and shape.
Only image-text pretraining is covered. Video, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer are not tested. The power-law form is not quantified even for image-text.
Downstream metrics are reported at only two sizes (115M/340M). There is no predictability analysis.
No comparison of fitting choices or exponents. No analysis of curvature.

missing.what: Joint perplexity at 115M vs 340M for both models across four validation sets. Larger models have lower perplexity, but there are only two sizes, so no power-law test is possible. Context only.
The compute budgets C_i and any fitted exponents are not stated anywhere in the text, including Appendix C, which lists only model variants.

record.verdict_notes: No verdicts are given. Every row linked to V3 or V5 is figure-only, with no stated exponents, loss values or curve-shape description, so all states remain cannot_determine. The caption does say scaling laws were fitted for both models, and a figure reading could support V5 and part of V3 in an image-text discrete-diffusion setting. UniDisc loss is an upper bound while AR loss is exact, which also biases the 13.2x comparison.

versions.untested_parts: The tested models jointly model images and text; the study does not test the stated scaling law for language models.
No result tests whether fits on small runs predict runs orders of magnitude larger.

The study plots fitted compute-optimal parameter counts, but does not report an explicit exponent or test whether optimal token counts follow a stable power of compute, or compare whether parameter growth is faster or equal to token growth.
No controlled comparison holds parameter count fixed while varying depth, width, or other architecture details.
The scaling analysis is for joint text-image models. It does not test video or other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer as scaling regimes.
Downstream task results are not tested for predictability from scale or pretraining loss.
The study does not test how fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocations vary with fitting choices, nor whether curves bend away from power laws.
